title: Dysphagia: Pattern & Workup
subtitle: Localize symptoms, separate obstruction from motility & choose the next test

sections.heading: Localize first
items: Oropharyngeal: trouble initiating a swallow, with cough, drooling, dysarthria or nasal regurgitation.
Esophageal: food feels stuck after swallowing; evaluation then focuses on structural and motor causes.

sections.heading: Use the food pattern
items: Solids more than liquids suggests a structural narrowing: ring, web, stricture, tumor or EoE.
Solids and liquids suggests a motility disorder such as achalasia, spasm or hypercontractile esophagus.

sections.heading: Choose the next test
items: Oropharyngeal symptoms: modified barium swallow plus speech-language/ENT assessment as appropriate.
Esophageal dysphagia: upper endoscopy is central; barium esophagram can provide complementary anatomy.
If endoscopy is unrevealing and obstruction persists, high-resolution manometry evaluates motor disorders.

sections.heading: EoE: current update
items: Diagnosis: esophageal dysfunction plus >=15 eosinophils/hpf, after evaluating other causes of eosinophilia.
ACG 2025 advises >=6 targeted biopsies from 2 esophageal levels and standardized endoscopic assessment.
First-line options include PPI, swallowed topical steroid or empiric elimination diet; use shared decisions.

callout: Food impaction that cannot pass or be brought back up warrants emergency evaluation.
